label: The sk-code compiler has no ranking logic: the authored tieBreak is copied verbatim into every compiled artifact at four sites — buildCompositionRules (:187, called :338), buildBundleRules (:227, called :261), and the routing-model copy (:265). Order enters as authored data and leaves as data.

A sibling hub already mints a DERIVED tieBreak: sk-doc compiles tieBreak: scoreTieBreakOrder(input.hubRouter) (:357) with the drift explanation at :188-196 (legacy replay reads routerSignals key order, the authored tieBreak array has drifted from it) — the in-tree precedent for option (c).

Insertion position decides the tie and validation does not constrain it: tieBreak lists opencode ahead of both examples (hub-router.json:7); the sibling completeness checks compare mode sets, not order (cli-classifier :165-168, sk-doc :115-120), so a user surface appended after opencode is valid but loses every tie.

--surface-hint is runtime-only and matched-only: compiled-route.cjs :99-108 applies the hint after validation to matched targets; resolve.cjs :102-108 passes it through; tests prove a matched hint leads (:68-77), an unmatched/UNKNOWN hint changes nothing (:79-83), and the front door passes the flag (:104-113). It works today as an opt-in complement but cannot be the shipped default.

Any order change must regenerate hand-authored canary fixtures and hint-test expectations: canary-cases.v1.json :117-127 no-hint expects [opencode, webflow]; :129-140 hinted expects [webflow, opencode]; the hint test asserts orders at :65, :72, :76, :89.

Recommended cheapest move: a rank field per surface in mode-registry.json delivered through a derived tieBreak at mint (registry-compiler.cjs :261, :265, :338; sk-doc precedent :357). Docs-only insertion fails (two drifting lists, unenforced position, stale-manifest stub), derivation alone fails (position still decides), the native boolean fails (one flag cannot give two repos different orders); shared prerequisite is a working re-mint for the external tree (carried P1).

direction: Docs-only insertion convention (insert before sk-code-opencode in tieBreak + routerSignals)
reason: Two lists must agree and have already drifted in a sibling hub (sk-doc :188-196); insertion position is unenforced; hand edit without a working re-mint serves the legacy stub (carried P1).

direction: Hardcoded native-last rule in the shared compiler or runtime
reason: Forces the operator's repo to the same order; the operator/external split is data today (Q4).
Confirmed blocked, not re-entered: matched-only reorder (:79-83), opt-in per call, cannot be the shipped default.
